source: ChEMBL REST API (www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/api/data) + UniProt REST fasta

molecule_molecule_chembl_id__in.note: the discriminator is total_count: an ignored __in filter would report the whole compound table (millions), a working one reports at most the ids asked for. An id in `requested` that no longer exists is therefore not a filter failure.

selection_rule: human SINGLE PROTEIN targets whose pref_name contains 'kinase', first 2000 in API order counted for exact-standard Ki rows (standard_type=Ki, standard_flag=1, standard_relation='='), panel = top 16 by that count, >= 300 such rows required

row_sampling.note: 'spread' takes evenly spaced 1000-row pages across the target's own result range with spacing floored at one page so pages cannot overlap; 'head' takes the first pages. A target is 'complete' when every usable row was fetched, otherwise the fetched/usable ratio is the sample fraction.

panel.pref_name: Mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase kinase 1

panel_candidates.pref_name: cAMP-dependent protein kinase catalytic subunit alpha

label_definition: pKi = 9 - log10(median Ki / nM); same 9-log10(nM) scale as DAVIS pKd, not comparable to KIBA's 0-17.2 consensus score
aggregation: median of the curated Ki rows for one (ligand, target) pair; n_rows / ki_iqr_nM carried alongside so the aggregation is auditable
temporal_proxy: document year from /document/{id}.json (ChEMBL's public API has no per-activity deposition date). This is a substitution, not the same quantity as DAVIS's deposited date.

sequence_verification.note: a UniProt record is used only if the fasta header accession equals the one ChEMBL reported and the OS= field equals --organism

transfer.bytes_this_process_only: bytes_downloaded counts this process only: pages already in data/raw/chembl/ are served from the disk cache and cost nothing here, so a re-run after a sampler change is nearly free while the first pull of the panel paid the bytes. The download cap the user authorised is on the whole job, so the size of everything actually held on disk is reported next to it.

raw_page_cache: data/raw/chembl/ (gitignored); every page this run read is cached and its sha256 is listed in raw_cache_sha256 below
